target.title: refactor(errors): consolidate shared error formatting
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Error formatting had drifted across core, gateway, plugin-runtime, and memory-host boundaries. Depending on the call site, the same failure could lose nested causes or codes, omit structured status details, or use a different redaction policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one structural formatter to `@openclaw/normalization-core` and makes the core and memory-host modules thin adapters that inject their owner-specific redactors. Gateway formatting now reuses the core adapter; three remaining generic core call sites do the same. The unused web-channel runtime formatter delegate is removed, while WhatsApp's formatter stays plugin-owned because it decodes Boom envelopes and transport-specific disconnect shapes.

AI-assisted: implemented and reviewed with Codex. I understand the ownership and behavior changes in this patch.

## User Impact

No new user-facing feature. Operators and developers get more consistent, redacted diagnostics with preserved cause chains and structured status/code details. Rich top-level diagnostic records retain their JSON fields instead of collapsing to status/code shorthand; arbitrary object causes preserve prior behavior. Non-test code decreases by 10 lines.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxct2cvhgxya2cghq2701tm1`: focused normalization, memory-host, infra, gateway, CLI, provider-classifier, and plugin-runtime suite passed 492 tests across six Vitest shards.
- Exact touched-file `oxfmt` and type-aware `oxlint`: passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: passed.
- `pnpm --filter @openclaw/normalization-core build`: passed, including declarations.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`: passed. The Plugin SDK surface gate is not applicable because no `src/plugin-sdk` file changed.
- Fresh autoreview: zero findings; patch correct at 0.84 confidence.
- `git diff --numstat` excluding tests: 122 additions, 132 deletions, net -10 non-test lines.

Known baseline gap: `pnpm check:changed` stops at the current-main TypeScript LOC ratchet on unrelated oversized files. Both touched oversized files are reported as smaller (`baseline-stale`), and the exact touched-surface checks above pass.
